items.q: What challenges do you support individuals with?
items.a: I support people navigating stress, overwhelm and burnout, life transitions, relationships, questions of identity and direction, the realities of international life, and personal growth. Many of my clients are high-functioning people who look like they have it all together but feel stretched thin underneath. Counselling gives you a calm, confidential space to slow down, make sense of what you are carrying, and move forward with more clarity.

items.q: Can counselling help with burnout and overwhelm?
items.a: Yes. Feeling constantly depleted, running on empty, or unable to switch off is something many capable people experience, and it is worth taking seriously. In counselling we gently explore what is draining you, what your overwhelm is telling you, and how to rebuild your energy and boundaries. The aim is to help you feel more grounded, resourced, and in tune with what matters to you.

items.q: I'm high-functioning but exhausted — is this for me?
items.a: Absolutely. Many people who come to me are successful and dependable on the outside while feeling tired, stretched, or disconnected within. You do not need to be in crisis to benefit from counselling. This is a space where you can set down the pressure to keep performing and focus on your own wellbeing for a change.

items.q: Can counselling help with a major life transition?
items.a: Yes. Big changes such as a new role, a move abroad, becoming a parent, the end of a relationship, or an uncertain next chapter can leave you feeling unsettled even when the change is a positive one. Counselling offers steady support while you find your footing and reconnect with your own direction. Together we make room to reflect, adjust, and step forward at a pace that feels right for you.

items.q: Can counselling help me with identity and direction?
items.a: Yes. Questions like who am I now, what do I really want, and where do I belong come up often, especially during transitions or after years of putting others first. Counselling gives you space to explore these questions honestly and without pressure. My aim is to help you reconnect with your own values and sense of direction so your choices feel more like your own.

items.q: Can counselling help me manage stress?
items.a: Yes. When stress builds up over time it can affect how you sleep, think, relate to others, and feel day to day. In counselling we look at what is fuelling your stress and explore practical, sustainable ways to steady yourself. Over time many clients find they feel calmer, clearer, and more able to respond to life rather than simply react to it.
